issue_text:
Hi, I need help with a few connected travel items, and I want complete details at each step for my records.

Please start by reviewing reservation 385BB3 and give me the full rundown: itinerary, cabin, passenger name, baggage allowance, insurance, status, booking date, and the payment details on file.
summary: A nine-turn travel-reservation session that opens with two stumbles and recovers into strong scope discipline. The agent first cannot find reservation 385BB3 and asks for a user ID (T1), then leaks a raw 500 Internal Server Error to the user verbatim (T2), before recovering at T3 to deliver the full booking rundown. It then reviews a second reservation (T4) and the customer profile (T5). The back half is the agent's best work: it declines the flight-search request (T6), works the fare comparison honestly — stating it has insufficient pricing data rather than inventing a number (T7) — and enumerates eleven out-of-scope document/inbox/calendar/email/spreadsheet tasks for a human handoff (T7-T8), while also admitting no transfer tool exists and instead building a copy-paste handoff summary. As a CONTROL baseline, the notable uncorrected defect is T2: a bare HTTP 500 stack reference is surfaced to the user with no reflection or retry framing, and the T3 recovery never acknowledges the error. The reservation figures (T3-T5) are also asserted on turns the component_timeline shows firing only generic other calls.

findings.title: A leaked 500 error, never reflected on
findings.body: T2's entire thought is a raw 500 Internal Server Error URL dump passed straight to the user. There is no Reflection move around it, and the T3 recovery opens with "I now have all the details" as if the failure never happened — the error is uncorrected in the sense that it is never acknowledged.

findings.title: Honest 'insufficient data' instead of a fabricated fare
findings.body: T7's fare-comparison paragraph is the set's cleanest Evaluate move: "I do not have enough pricing data to calculate a fare difference" — a Recognize-Knowledge-Boundary rather than the confident-but-ungrounded numbers seen in other baseline traces.

findings.title: Scope refusals cluster in the back half
findings.body: T6-T8 carry nearly all the Deciding › Decline and Evaluate › Recognize-Knowledge-Boundary tags — flight search, eleven document/office tasks, and the missing transfer tool are each declined explicitly, contrasting sharply with the ungrounded confidence of T3-T5.
